situation:
You are to assume the role of director of guest experience at SMOKESTACK ROW BARBECUE, a counter-serve barbecue chain with ninety restaurants. The vice president of operations (judge) has asked to meet with you about the self-order kiosks the company is already committed to installing.

SMOKESTACK ROW BARBECUE bought PINEY FORK BBQ eight months ago and is still running the two chains on separate schedules and separate training. Before that sale closed, PINEY FORK BBQ signed a three-year contract with BRIGHT COUNTER SYSTEMS for self-order kiosks in every restaurant by next spring, and the payments are owed whether or not the kiosks are installed.

In the same merger, the company promised its counter crews in writing that no restaurant would cut counter hours for two years, and installing the kiosks cuts those hours. The company's advertising also tells guests that someone who knows the meat greets them at the counter, and that greeting is the brand promise every campaign is built on.

Beef and labor costs have risen sharply for two years, and the kiosks would offset part of that. Installing them on the vendor's schedule would break the written promise to the counter crews and take away the counter greeting. Delaying the rollout would keep both, while the company pays BRIGHT COUNTER SYSTEMS for kiosks it is not using and absorbs the rising costs.

The vice president of operations (judge) wants you to recommend one course and explain what the company owes each side. The vice president (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the vice president's (judge's) questions, the vice president (judge) will thank you for your work.
